'''Wiebke Drenckhan''', born 6 April 1977 in [[Bad Belzig]], is a [[Germans|German]] [[physicist]]. She is a [[French National Centre for Scientific Research|CNRS]] research director at the [[Institut Charles Sadron]], where she investigates the physics and physical chemistry of liquid and solid [[foam]]s and [[emulsion]]s. She also works as illustrator for scientific journals and popular science books and she collaborates regularly with artists and designers.

== Biography==
After studying physics and mathematics in Germany ([[University of Rostock]], [[Humboldt University of Berlin|Humboldt University Berlin]]) and New Zealand ([[University of Canterbury]]) she joins  [[Trinity College Dublin]] for her PhD thesis under the supervision of [[Denis Weaire]].<ref>{{Cite thesis|title=Stability and motion of foams and films in confined geometries|url=http://www.tara.tcd.ie/handle/2262/86304|publisher=Trinity College (Dublin, Ireland). School of Physics|date=2005|degree=thesis|language=en|first=Wiebke|last=Drenckhan|hdl=2262/86304 }}</ref> In the following, she receives an EMBARK Fellowship from the Irish Research Council, before being invited on a 1-year research stay by the city of Paris to work at the [[Paris Diderot University|University Paris-Diderot]]. In 2007, she is hired by the [[French National Centre for Scientific Research|CNRS]] and joins [[Dominique Langevin]]’s research group at the Laboratoire de Physique des Solides at [[Paris-Sud University]]. In 2014 she obtains her [[Habilitation#France|Habilitation à Diriger les Recherches]] on the topic “A science of transition – from liquid to solid foams”. In 2016, she moves her research activities to the [[Institut Charles Sadron]] at the [[University of Strasbourg]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=WIEBKE'S WEBSITE|url=https://www.ics-cnrs.unistra.fr/drenckhan/main/|access-date=2021-08-16|website=www.ics-cnrs.unistra.fr|archive-date=2021-08-16|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210816082611/https://www.ics-cnrs.unistra.fr/drenckhan/main/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

== Research ==
Wiebke Drenckhan works on the physics and physical chemistry of liquid and solid foams and emulsions.<ref>{{Cite web|last=ORCID|title=Wiebke Drenckhan (0000-0002-3879-4956)|url=https://orcid.org/0000-0002-3879-4956|access-date=2021-08-16|website=orcid.org|language=en}}</ref> Linking fundamental and applied research, she combines experiments and computer simulations to advance our understanding of the generation, stability and structure of liquid foams and emulsions. She uses this understanding to propose new approaches for the generation of solid polymer foams with controlled structural properties in a “liquid templating” approach, with the goal to understand and control their structure-property relations. Of particular interest to her work is the development of interfacial mechanisms to modify in a controlled manner how bubbles and drops interact in foams and emulsions in order to create self-assembled polymeric [[metamaterial]]s. 

== Awards==

* 2012 [[European Research Council|ERC]] Starting Grant
* 2013 [[Irène Joliot-Curie Prize]] for “Young French Female Scientist of the Year”<ref>{{Cite web|title=With the Académie des Sciences in 2013–2014|url=https://www.academie-sciences.fr/pdf/documentation/RA3gb/files/assets/basic-html/page-15.html#|access-date=2021-08-16|website=www.academie-sciences.fr}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Prix Irène Joliot-Curie 2013 : Wiebke Drenckhan, Prix de la "Jeune Femme scientifique" – Vidéo Dailymotion|url=https://www.dailymotion.com/video/x17f4dz|access-date=2021-08-16|website=Dailymotion|date=20 November 2013 |language=en}}</ref>
* 2013 Henkel Laundry & Home Care Research Award<ref>{{Cite web|last=Henkel|title=Award-winning foam research|url=https://www.henkel.com/press-and-media/press-releases-and-kits/2013-07-12-press-release-award-winning-foam-research-27902|access-date=2021-08-16|website=www.henkel.com|language=en|archive-date=2021-08-16|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210816082611/https://www.henkel.com/press-and-media/press-releases-and-kits/2013-07-12-press-release-award-winning-foam-research-27902|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* 2015 CNRS Bronze Medal<ref>{{Cite web|title=Wiebke Drenckhan {{!}} CNRS|url=https://www.cnrs.fr/fr/personne/wiebke-drenckhan|access-date=2021-08-16|website=www.cnrs.fr|date=January 2015 |language=fr}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=EDP Sciences – Wiebke Drenckhan, EDP Sciences books' illustrator gets the CNRS Bronze Medal|url=https://www.edpsciences.org/en/news-highlights/248-wiebke-drenckhan-edp-sciences-books-illustrator-gets-the-cnrs-bronze-medal-2015-03-24|access-date=2021-08-16|website=www.edpsciences.org}}</ref>
* 2019 [[European Research Council|ERC]] Consolidator grant

== Outreach ==
Wiebke Drenckhan is actively involved in different scientific outreach activities.<ref>{{Citation|title=Un témoignage : Wiebke Drenckhan et sa passion pour les mousses|url=https://vimeo.com/88231900|language=en|access-date=2021-08-16}}</ref><ref>{{Citation|title=Variations sur une bulle – Les Curieuses Rencontres| date=28 April 2021 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HBwSdM6Gy5U|language=en|access-date=2021-08-16}}</ref><ref>{{Citation|title=WIEBKE DRENCKHAN – Rencontres Internationales Corps-Objet-Image 2019|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FGcT6upJLJg|language=en|access-date=2021-08-16}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Wiebke Drenckhan – Portrait de "Femmes en physique" – Vidéo Dailymotion|url=https://www.dailymotion.com/video/x2brcmz|access-date=2021-08-16|website=Dailymotion|date=4 December 2014 |language=en}}</ref> She collaborates regularly with artists and designers. She also works as cartoonist and illustrator for scientific journals and popular science books.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Café, crème, savon et Cie|url=https://laboutique.edpsciences.fr/produit/594/9782759808717/Cafe%20creme%20savon%20et%20Cie|access-date=2021-08-16|website=laboutique.edpsciences.fr|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Textiles, parfums, bijoux et Cie|url=https://laboutique.edpsciences.fr/produit/685/9782759812240/Textiles%20parfums%20bijoux%20et%20Cie|access-date=2021-08-16|website=laboutique.edpsciences.fr|language=en}}</ref> She provided for many years physics cartoons for the German [[Physik Journal]] and illustrated the “Physics in Daily life” Column by Jo Hermans in [[European Physical Society|Europhysics News]].
